item.title: Marvel Studios debuted a unique promo for Avengers: Doomsday during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series on Fox tonight between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. The ad is an Avengers-MLB crossover set on Earth-828 at Ebbets Field (the former home of the Dodgers when they were in Brooklyn; it was torn down on our Earth in 1960 – the promo is seemingly set in the same time period as The Fantastic Four: First Steps, as you can see New York Giants players in the background).
item.description:
Marvel Studios debuted a unique promo for Avengers: Doomsday during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series on Fox tonight between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. The ad is an Avengers-MLB crossover set on Earth-828 at Ebbets Field (the former home of the Dodgers when they were in Brooklyn; it was torn down on our Earth in 1960 – the promo is seemingly set in the same time period as The Fantastic Four: First Steps, as you can see New York Giants players in the background).
In it, Mr. Fantastic, sporting a Brooklyn Dodgers cap, takes the mound to throw a stretchy-armed first pitch while The Thing hypes up the players as current, modern MLB players Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Bryce Harper, Randy Arozarena, and Junior Caminero look on from the sidelines. They're interrupted when Dr. Doom attacks from the sky, with clips from the film interspersed throughout the promo.
Worlds collide ⚾An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 https://t.co/WX1YtKjAKt
Live sporting events, such as the Super Bowl, NBA Finals, and World Series remain one of Hollywood's favorite mediums to debut new trailers and promote films, as in the age of streaming and on-demand content, they're one of the few forms of programming that consistently drive a live, tuned-in audience.
Avengers: Doomsday returns Chris Evans as Steve Rogers (which is referenced in a clip from the film used in the MLB promo), while Robert Downey Jr. trades Iron Man's mask for Dr. Doom's and appears to be abducting heroes in the upcoming film (though we will see RDJ as Stark at least one more time, starting in 2028 at Disney California Adventure's upcoming Avengers: Infinity Defense ride). Much of it remains shrouded in mystery, such that even actors in the film don't know what happens.
Audience interest appears to be strong, as ticket pre-sales are outpacing those of this summer's blockbuster hit Spider-Man: Brand New Day. But Marvel recommends you do your homework before heading to the theater for Doomsday.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Three-time Emmy winner Aaron Paul has a blink and you’ll miss it cameo in the new DC movie Clayface. Now, the film’s director, James Watkins, has revealed why the Breaking Bad and Westworld star is in DC’s first R-rated horror movie.
item.description:
Spoilers follow for Clayface, which is now playing in theaters.
Three-time Emmy winner Aaron Paul has a blink and you’ll miss it cameo in the new DC movie Clayface. Now, the film’s director, James Watkins, has revealed why the Breaking Bad and Westworld star is in DC’s first R-rated horror movie.
Paul plays Jimmy “One Nut” Hagen, the late abusive father of protagonist Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries). Word of Paul’s casting was first reported by Feature First back in June.
Paul’s cameo occurs during the climactic action sequence set at the Gotham City nightclub Vesuvius where Matt confronts the gangsters who disfigured him. Matt finds the hood who killed his dad and morphs into his father to shock the killer.
Paul originally had a larger supporting role in Clayface, appearing in flashbacks to Matt’s youth, but the filmmakers ultimately cut nearly all of those scenes. Paul’s appearance in the nightclub is all that remains of his role.
“In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly.
“At one point, we were looking at it and thinking, Is it the ‘sins of the father’? But actually, as we worked on the script, I thought that notion of revenge was more universal and more relatable to all of us. It doesn’t matter whether you’re carrying a trauma or any of that. If we’re slighted, we carry this sense of being wronged and we all want to do something, but generally in life we can’t do anything about it and we’re powerless.”
As EW points out, rather than having Matt haunted by his dad he instead weaponizes the memory of his father against his enemies. “He’s probably also saying, ‘No, I’m not my father,’” said Watkins.
For more on the film, read my Clayface review, our Clayface ending explained, and catch up on everything we know so far about the DCU’s Batman.

item.title: Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
item.description:
Dead by Daylight fans are beside themselves after Behaviour Interactive announced that all Chucky content would no longer be available to purchase starting next month.
The developer behind the popular asymmetrical horror game confirmed plans to pull the Chucky Chapter from sale in posts shared across social media. The message followed rumors that the possessed killer doll would soon be removed from the game, with the official statement promising that those who have purchased related content will be able to use it even after it is removed from shelves starting November 24, 2026.
"We welcomed The Good Guy out of his box and into The Fog nearly three years ago, but it's now time for the Chucky Chapter to leave the shelf," Behaviour said. "On November 24, 2026, the Chapter and its associated content will be removed from in-game and first-party stores. Any content unlocked before that date will remain available to use in-game."
As detailed in an FAQ post shared by the developers, these changes to the Chucky Chapter mean a few things for Dead by Daylight players. Its Killer, known in-game as The Good Guy, will no longer be available to purchase, though bug fixes will still be supported. The collection of outfits and cosmetics he's gained since being added in 2023 will also be made unavailable, and no future add-ons for the character will be added.
In other words, if you're a Chucky fan who's been waiting to pull the trigger, you might want to start thinking about it. To help ease players into the idea of losing one of Dead by Daylight's most unique Killers, Behaviour is holding a sale for all items related to the Chucky Chapter starting Monday, October 26. The "Last Chance" sale runs until his November 24 removal date and slashes prices by 50% across all platforms.
Dead by Daylight and its collection of Killers has often been referred to as 'horror Super Smash Bros.' by fans, but Behaviour has plenty of experience when it comes to pulling Killers. Hellraiser's Pinhead was pulled from digital storefronts in 2025 after first joining in 2021. Halloween's Michael Myers, the first major playable Killer to join Dead by Daylight after its launch in 2016, was removed this past January.
@DeadbyDaylight I THOUGHT WE HAD A NICE LICENSE AGREEMENT!!!!! https://t.co/bOMgT44DQt
Although Behaviour refrained from sharing more details about why exactly the Child's Play rep is being removed, fans usually assume licensing issues are to blame. Hellraiser and Halloween both received new game announcements in Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival and Halloween: The Game that just happened to arrive around the time their respective properties were pulled from Dead by Daylight. Friday the 13th's infamous licensing kerfuffle is also allegedly what kept Jason Voorhees out of The Fog for years before he finally joined a few months back. Stranger Things is another example, with its first chapter's Demogorgon content removed before returning in 2023.
Like Chucky, players who purchased pulled content can still use it freely even after it's removed from stores, but that doesn't mean other players can't feel the impact. Content being removed from purchase not only means that players won't be able to buy it in the future; it means that content will likely show up less frequently during matches.
That affects just about everyone who likes having their Survivor matches shaken up by new Killer abilities to keep them on their toes, as a player doesn't need to have purchased a chapter to play against its respective Killer. Considering Michael Myers left Dead by Daylight earlier this year and Pinhead was removed not much longer before that, players are feeling Chucky's pull from sale more than many of the previous Killer removals.
"Hold a license challenge: impossible," one fan said.
"How do you keep losing licenses bro?" another fan speculated. "I thought you had a good relationship. Chucky had many skins WTF :("
goodbye chuckster. i will always love you https://t.co/h6sUaDGrwI
Again, Behaviour has not explicitly stated why new players will not be able to purchase Chucky after that November cutoff date. IGN has reached out to the Dead by Daylight team for comment.
"This makes me so sad," one player on Reddit said. "Chucky is such a huge license and we've lost Michael and Pinhead already within the last two years. Not blaming BHVR for it, I get it's business. It just sucks."
"It's strange though. You'd assume they'd change their contractual agreements after losing Demogorgon the first time to prevent this from happening with recent Killers," another replied. "Michael/Pinhead are a bit understandable since those were older licenses, but I'd assume Chucky would've had a proactive contractual agreement to prevent this from happening?"
Although losing three Killers in the span of a year and a half might sting, Behaviour has continued to add new notable characters and franchises into the mix. After Tokyo Ghoul's Ken Kaneki and Five Nights at Freddy's Springtrap were added last year, the studio brought Stranger Things villain Vecna into The Fog. Jason joined in the summer of this year, and Terrifier's Art the Clown will be added next month. Although the majority of the game's licensed Killers have remained available for years and are still available to this day, how long they will remain available for purchase is unclear.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.
item.description:
Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.
Information about the last-minute addition comes from The Hollywood Reporter, which said the Project Hail Mary star will appear on screens when Earth's Mightiest Heroes take on Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom this December. Although much of that cast and their parts in the movie have been confirmed, details about Hüller's role were not shared.
Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo almost certainly have plans for plenty of superhero moments and surprises. How Hüller fits into that plan remains to be seen, but considering fans had already speculated about her involvement in recent days, some of the less patient Marvel Cinematic Universe enjoyers are probably already doing their best to piece together Doomsday's mysteries early.
Hüller is a German actor with a decades-long career on movie and TV screens. She was nominated for Actress in a Leading Role at the 2024 Oscars for her part in Anatomy of a Fall, but is also known for her parts in films like Digger, The Zone of Interest, and Fatherland. If you missed her in any of those movies, there's a good chance you caught her playing Eva Stratt, a role that we called one of the best parts of Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary.
As for her Marvel introduction, all we know for now is that she'll appear in a cameo part, meaning she probably won't show up for much of its 2-hour-and-45-minute runtime. Like major stars – including Harry Styles and Charlize Theron – before her, it's possible that we could only see Hüller's character during a stinger moment shown during the film's credits sequence. There's at least little reason to suspect that's not on the table, especially considering Marvel will use Doomsday's plot to set up the release of Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027.
Doomsday is out in just a few short months, but that clearly hasn't stopped Marvel from revealing new information for what's gearing up to be one of the year's biggest releases. Even more about the movie is expected to be revealed at the MLB World Series, which is just a few hours after this piece's publication. THR noted that the Russo brothers are knee-deep in post-production for the film ahead of its December 18, 2026, premiere.
Avengers: Doomsday will bring the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more when it arrives in a few months. Until then, you can read what Jeremy Renner had to say about the good guys' chances without Hawkeye. You can also see how David Harbour did his best to walk back what may have been an early spoiler.
Photo by Matt Crossick/Variety via Getty Images.

item.title: Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, is no longer in the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.
item.description:
Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, is no longer in the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.
The memo, verified by The Verge, included a brief statement from Sharma regarding Chiang’s exit. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” Sharma said. “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”
Chiang had been with Xbox for an astonishing 21 years. Previously, she was in charge of the Minecraft franchise, and shifted roles to chief operating officer in July 2026.
The reason for Chiang’s promotion and the job duties of the COO were outlined in a statement by Sharma amid news of Xbox’s massive restructuring this summer. According to Sharma, the role was necessary to “work toward a shared goal, make the right tradeoffs, and get things done” as Xbox’s headcount grew and the company became “more fragmented.”
“For the first time, we are establishing a Chief Operating Officer with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. Helen Chiang has been promoted to this role and will report directly to me,” Sharma said at the time.
“Over nearly two decades at Xbox, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from Xbox Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”
As noted by The Verge, the reason for Chiang’s brief tenure in this specific role has not yet been divulged, but it’s certainly a striking move, given her 21 years with the company prior to this.
Xbox is predicted to continue layoffs as part of its ongoing internal restructuring, with 3,200 total employees expected to lose their jobs this year. Several studios have been divested as a result of this rework, though some have managed to find their footing, as is the case with Double Fine.
Others, however, remain in limbo; Arkane Lyon, the studio that’s currently working on Marvel’s Blade, faces closure as soon as mid-November if a buyer isn’t found. The studio was also impacted by the reshuffling at Microsoft, leaving both fans and industry insiders biting their nails in hope that the project finds a new home.
Other companies in the games industry aren’t faring any better. Just this week, EA announced the closure of 30-year-old RPG powerhouse BioWare, known for making games like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, and Mass Effect. The next Mass Effect game was also canceled, prompting worldwide outcry from players and calls for a boycott.
A full-length trailer for the game was also leaked online, rubbing more salt in the wound thanks to just how fantastic it looked. And while fans are crossing their fingers that EA either sells BioWare’s IP or hands them over to another studio, analysts say this isn’t likely. Oh, well — at least the Prime Video series is still alive.

item.title: The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has removed the game from online marketplaces and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its homeless people as ‘zombies.’
item.description:
The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has taken down the game and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its citizens as ‘zombies.’
Tenderloin Night Shift was a vibe-coded, first-person shooter created by independent developer Pierre-Louis Biojout over the course of a weekend using OpenAI’s Codex. As you’ve probably inferred by its title, the game takes place in San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood, an area infamous for its high crime rates and unhoused population that’s often compared offhandedly to Los Angeles’s Skid Row.
In the game, players use a gun to rid the Tenderloin of ‘zombies.’ Some of these undead enemies wear construction uniforms or whiz by on motorized scooters, while others wear food delivery backpacks, having clearly been infected while on the job. Still others are depicted doing the ‘fentanyl fold,’ a position where the body is bent forward at the waist, most usually displayed by fentanyl users who seem to have been frozen while standing upright.
“San Francisco couldn’t fix the tenderloin, so I monetized it,” Biojout said on social media. In the game, he sold digital ad space for $100 per week, which accounts for some of the real-world companies seen on billboards within his polygonal recreation of the neighborhood.
It didn’t take long for San Francisco city officials to take notice of the title. Speaking to NCB Bay Area, Mayor Daniel Lurie said, “There’s no accounting for taste or people’s terrible ideas. This is a bad one, and we reject it. It doesn’t speak for San Francisco values.”
In a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle, Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin, dubbed the game “deeply disturbing and unacceptable.”
“Turning violence against real people, including unhoused people, into entertainment is dehumanizing and should never be normalized,” he said. “I’m encouraged to see that the majority of San Franciscans recognize that this crosses a line and refuse to stand for it.”
While Biojout was previously boasting about the backlash on his social media accounts, he later removed the game from his online platform and issued a public apology over how his project depicted San Francisco’s citizens. He also revealed that he’d been inspired by an Alcatraz-themed Call of Duty map and said he often passes by the Tenderloin on his way to work.
“The game was not intended to provoke or to depict shooting real people. Its characters draw on a broad cross-section of San Francisco, across different backgrounds and walks of life, including people who work in tech. The familiar city details and Easter eggs are part of what makes it fun to play with friends,” he told the Chronicle.
Speaking to NBC Bay Area, Bijout said, “It was not intended to depict shooting real people or to target a particular demographic or group.”
Additionally, Biojout revealed that he refunded advertisers who promoted his game and removed all of his social media posts about it. He also donated the game’s total revenue to the Delancey Street Foundation, a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco that provides rehabilitation services and vocational training to convicted criminals and those suffering from substance abuse.
“I built and posted a zombie game set on San Francisco streets. The setting and the way I promoted it showed poor judgment. Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention,” he wrote on Twitter/X.
The game was available on Biojout's NanoCorp AI website, a platform that runs online businesses using AI agents. It has since been removed, and the page is no longer available at the time of writing.

item.title: Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as "Chani" in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.
item.description:
Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as Chani in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.
“The move marks a shift from the first two films, where she was positioned in supporting actress,” said Variety. “The decision reflects Chani’s expanded role in the story.”
This larger, different role for Zendaya’s character in Dune: Part III has not gone unnoticed. IGN’s Jesse Schedeen recently wrote that “everything we’ve seen of Dune: Part Three so far suggests Chani is playing a vastly different role compared to the source material [Frank Herbert’s book Dune Messiah]. Her status quo is completely different. She isn’t Paul’s faithful concubine, pining for the day she can proudly bear his children. She’s rejected Paul and everything he stands for, preferring instead to live as a true Fremen, totally free and a servant to no one.”
It should be noted that none of the actors in either of the past two Dune movies have earned either an Oscar or a Golden Globe nomination for those films. Both Dune movies, however, were nominated in technical categories.
Zendaya has enjoyed a stellar year as an actor, earning praise for The Drama and starring in the two highest-grossing movies of 2026, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey.
The leading entertainment industry awards prognosticators at GoldDerby, however, don’t have Zendaya as a hopeful in either of the Oscars’ actress categories for any of her films. (They currently have her Odyssey co-stars Anne Hathaway and Samantha Morton as the leading contenders to earn a Best Supporting Actress nomination for that film.)
GoldDerby does, however, have Zendaya in the running for a Golden Globe nomination as Best Film Comedy/Musical Actress for The Drama and as TV Drama Actress for the final season of Euphoria. They also have her in the running for a Screen Actors Guild nomination as TV Drama Actress for Euphoria.
The Academy recently altered their rules ahead of next year’s Oscars, including updating their positions on AI and allowing multiple nominations for the same actor in the same category.
The 99th Academy Awards will air live on ABC and Hulu on Sunday, March 14, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. It will be the third year in a row that Conan O’Brien has hosted the Oscars ceremony.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: A sequel to Ridley Scott's Alien: Covenant is reportedly in the works with Prisoners writer Aaron Guzikowski.
item.description:
A follow-up to Ridley Scott's Alien: Covenant is reportedly in the works with Prisoners writer Aaron Guzikowski.
A continuation of the sci-fi horror franchise has started to pick up steam, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Scott is in the mix as a producer, with Guzikowski, who previously worked with Scott on HBO's Raised by Wolves, set to pen its script.
The new Alien film seems to be in its early stages, with much of its plot remaining a secret for now. However, the report did state that it will not be a sequel to 2024's Alien: Romulus and is instead expected to share ties with Scott's Prometheus and Alien: Covenant films. The plan is for its story to include Michael Fassbender's David, though the actor is not attached to return quite yet.
No director has been chosen for now, with Scott only involved as a producer along with Scott Free's Michael Pruss. THR said Scott specifically went to Guzikowski to help get the ball rolling on the project, which he announced in August.
Although there is much work to be done, there is no doubt a large section of Scott fans who will be happy to see more from David the Android. Fassbender first played the character in 2012's Prometheus before returning for its Covenant sequel in 2017. As other Alien projects have come and gone in the years since, how Scott might finish his offshoot trilogy largely remained a mystery.
As for Alien: Romulus, a sequel to the Cailee Spaeny and David Jonsson-starring horror movie was said to still be in limbo. Scott said in August that he thought the first film "was OK" when confirming he intended to return to the franchise because it "needs some help." Although a proper follow-up was said to be in the works as of late 2024, all we've really heard since then is that Fede Alvarez would produce – not direct – whatever came next.
For now, information about the next Alien movie's cast and plot is unclear. While we wait for Scott and Guzikowski to deliver updates, you can read about the long history of Alien and Predator crossovers.

item.title: Mass Effect fans are calling for a boycott of all EA products and services in protest of the company closing down BioWare and canceling the next Mass Effect game.
item.description:
Mass Effect fans are calling for a boycott of all EA products and services in protest of the company closing down BioWare and canceling the next Mass Effect game.
It’s a rough time for Mass Effect fans. On October 21, EA announced its plans to shut down BioWare, a 30-year-old studio that spearheaded RPGs in the West with titles like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, Baldur’s Gate, and of course, Mass Effect.
Players were eagerly awaiting news of the next game in BioWare’s beloved sci-fi franchise — but EA shut that down, too, revealing in a statement that the project was officially canceled.
In the two days since then, fans of BioWare and the Mass Effect series have gathered together to call for action, begging EA to at least sell off BioWare’s IP to other studios rather than letting them languish. In fact, tensions have become so strained that players are now calling for an outright boycott of EA’s products and services until something is done.
On Reddit, several threads are rallying Mass Effect fans to gather under the hashtag #savemasseffect, urging players to take action and make their voices heard.
“WE HAVE TO DO SOMETHING! Guys we have to start something here and cry out loud enough that this game can be saved. Either EA making it or selling it off. We have to do it now before the noise on this game quiets down and it becomes another cancelled series, never to return,” one Redditor wrote. “I suggest we start a movement, and message the hell out of EA asking for some kind of outcome that gets this game finished. THIS GAME FINISHED.”
“Mass Effect is one of the better RPGs out today,” another fan wrote in a post titled ‘EA Boycott!’ “...Unless they sell Mass Effect to another studio or bring it back. I will never buy another EA product ever. They are already not one of my favorite studios. No more Respawn Entertainment, DICE, Motive Studios, Criterion Games, Maxis, Full Circle, Cliffhanger Games, or any EA Sports.
“I hope I'm not alone in this. We need to stand up and make our voices heard. I posted on everything I can. We can't let Mass Effect die so easily. Private investors need to realize how badly EA screwed up.”
These calls for a boycott coincide with a fanmade petition urging EA to either sell off the IPs to other developers or hand development of Mass Effect 5 to a different studio. At the time of writing, this petition has garnered over 76,500 signatures and counting as more fans and friends of the industry pile in.
Mass Effect 5 — which was reportedly expected to be called Mass Effect Universe — seems to have already been a good way into its development cycle, judging by a full-length trailer that was leaked online yesterday. This trailer rubbed even more salt in the wound for players, many of whom believed this game would be everything fans had been asking for and more.
Industry vets and even voice actors from the Mass Effect games are speaking out in hopes of somehow, some way, getting this game on shelves. But according to industry analysts and former BioWare bosses, it’s not likely that EA will listen to fans’ demands.

item.title: The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.
item.description:
The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.
PlayStation 5 sales have jumped by 22%, according to a report from Bloomberg, with data from Circana. And, while it's likely that the buildup to GTA 6 has contributed to those sales, it looks like it was September's all-star lineup of games, and particularly Marvel's Wolverine, that were primarily behind the PS5's recent success.
We reached out to Circana Senior Director and Video Game Industry Advisor Mat Piscatella for comment on these recent sales increases, and he told us that despite its middling reception, Wolverine drove quite a bit of hardware sales. "PS5's hardware boost was primarily driven by Marvel's Wolverine. NBA 2K27 and Grand Theft Auto VI also likely helped," he said. However, he added that "Xbox Series did not get a similar sales boost during the month."
When IGN reviewed Wolverine, we gave it a middling 6 out of 10, with reviewer Simon Cardy saying, "Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay."
In the weeks that have followed the game's release, the community has also been mixed on the game, and Insomniac has had to respond by fixing some of the more hand-holdy mechanics, like adding a toggle for the ever-present scent trail that guides you to objectives. But, even early on, there were signs that Wolverine was selling.
Now, more than a month after release, Wolverine seems like it was absolutely a success, with Piscatella saying, "For Marvel's Wolverine, [it's] tough to give things a vibe check without understanding folks' frame of reference, but it was the month's best-seller, ranks 11th year-to-date, with a hardware bundle that seems to have sold out and the market's best-selling accessory during the month with the limited edition Marvel's Wolverine DualSense. Seems pretty good to me. But, we'll have to see how the legs are over time. It wasn't as big as say Marvel's Spider-Man 2, but I don't think that would have ever been a reasonable assumption."
That hardware bundle was likely a big reason why PlayStation's sales were so rosy over the last month. The controller looked amazing, and started selling out before the game even launched.
Looking ahead to GTA 6, though, if a game like Wolverine was able to drive hardware like this, I can only imagine that GTA is going to make an even bigger impact. We've already started to see signs of that happening, too. Just a couple of weeks ago, the PS5 Pro started selling out enough that used models started going for as much as $1,400, $500 more than their shelf price. And, to this day, that price still holds, with the PS5 Pro available on both Amazon and Gamestop for $1,399.
At that price, it's going to be interesting to see sales data for this coming month, and how many people are willing to fork over that kind of cash for a new console. After all, there have been rumors this week that the next-generation Xbox Project Helix may cost up to $1,800. There were also leaks that suggest that for the PS6, just the RAM and SSD alone will cost around $680, which could see Sony's next-gen console commanding a similar price.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the first three Mass Effect games, is speaking out after a leaked trailer for the sci-fi franchise’s next title was leaked online.
item.description:
Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the first three Mass Effect games, is speaking out after a leaked trailer for the sci-fi franchise’s next title was leaked online.
The Mass Effect community was hit hard this week by news that EA is closing down BioWare, the 30-year-old studio known for spearheading Western RPGs with series like Dragon Age, Mass Effect, Jade Empire, and others.
Rubbing salt in the wound, EA also revealed the next Mass Effect game (supposedly titled Mass Effect Universe) was canceled. This revelation hurt even more after staff who formerly worked on the project spoke out about it online, with one even leaking a full-length trailer for the game on Reddit. This trailer promised a game that would have been everything fans wanted and more — and it even caught the attention of FemShep herself.
Hale responded to a re-upload of the Mass Effect 5 trailer on X/Twitter, and it seems she’s just as hopeful as the rest of us that somehow, some way, the game will still get made.
“It's extraordinary,” she wrote. “I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible devs deserve that and more.”
Two days prior, she went live on Instagram alongside fellow Commander Shepard voice actor Mark Meer, who plays the male version of the character, to address fans in the wake of EA’s devastating decision
“I feel weirdly hopeful, and I can’t explain why,” Hale said. “...I feel for the [BioWare] employees who are suddenly unemployed. That is the number one thing on my mind. Those beautiful team members who are looking for a new home.”
“It is very sad news,” Meer added. “It is a massive loss for Edmonton, for Canada, and for the video game industry in general. It’s very unfortunate to see. And of course, I feel very bad for all of the fans.”
“It’s really hard to think about BioWare being shut down, but it was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is,” Hale continued. “And I’m hopeful that maybe, there might be some crazy thing where they decide that. in order to increase their profit margins — which is often their priority — they will release these IPs into the market to sell them, and use that to do what they do, which is increase their profit margins. But maybe, someone could grab hold of these IPs and do something with them.”
Hale isn’t alone in this line of thinking; many fans are calling on EA to at least sell BioWare’s intellectual properties to other developers in the hopes that Mass Effect 5 can eventually be released. Even Canadian politicians are getting in on the conversation, with the country’s New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis taking to social media to publicly call out EA.
However, industry insiders and analysts are urging caution around this particular idea. Speaking with IGN, three separate analysts stated that BioWare’s library of titles simply don’t align with EA’s current strategy, and said it’s unlikely the company relinquishes them to other companies. What’s more, these IPs are likely to be extremely expensive, to the point where other studios simply wouldn’t have the funds nor the time to pursue them.
Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah shared a similar sentiment, though he admitted that, given EA is now looking to cut costs to cover its massive debt, it might consider the idea of selling these IPs off — but said it’s just as likely that execs “just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.”
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Xbox reportedly asked Netflix for $800 million for a seven-year deal that would have given the streamer exclusive adaptations based on its games.
item.description:
Xbox reportedly asked Netflix for $800 million for a seven-year deal that would have given the streamer exclusive adaptations based on its games.
Details on the behind-the-scenes dealings between the two entertainment giants came from a Puck report. The site stated that Netflix, interested in pursuing movie and TV adaptations for some of Microsoft's biggest games, began its offer at $500 million.
What exactly the deal would have yielded outside of the promise to exclusively-licensed Xbox titles for adaptations is unclear, but for Microsoft, it was worth a lot more than what Netflix was willing to offer. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and her team countered the offer at a staggering $800 million. Following a round of shakeups at Netflix from last week, the deal is said to be completely off the table.
It's unclear what exactly led to the deal breaking down, though Puck suggested the exit of Bela Bajaria, who served as content chief until being fired recently, played a role. Now, the site said that Xbox is "pursuing smaller deals with more partners." Who those partners are is a mystery for now.
While Xbox and Netflix were unable to secure a long-term exclusivity deal, both entertainment entities do have plans to work together in the future. A live-action movie and animated series based on Gears of War, for example, have been in the works for some time. In 2024, Netflix announced it was building a Minecraft animated series, and just last month, plans for an animated Diablo series were confirmed.
Xbox shared a statement with Puck: "We have received record-breaking interest in our IP; Netflix is a valued partner and we are excited for the forthcoming release of our Minecraft and Diablo animated series together, among other adaptations."
Netflix announced layoffs impacting around 1,000 staff earlier this month. A few high-profile executives, including Bajaria, were fired just days later. The list also included head of film Dan Lin, who reportedly recently clashed with Barbie director Greta Gerwig about the release of her upcoming Netflix film, Narnia: The Magician's Nephew.
Whether Xbox can manage to find partners for more movie and TV adaptations remains to be seen. In the meantime, you can check out what IGN thought of a few other recent video game adaptations. Capcom's Street Fighter movie, for example, received a 6/10 review, while its Resident Evil movie managed to earn an 8/10.

item.title: Following the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe, last week – alongside the closure of the entire BioWare development studio – new gameplay details about the role-playing game revival have emerged, including handcrafted missions that gave players Hitman-style freedom, the abililty to hack the environment, brutal close-range executions, the return of Liara, and much more.
item.description:
Following this week's cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe – alongside the closure of the entire BioWare development studio – new gameplay details about the role-playing game revival have emerged, including handcrafted missions that gave players Hitman-style freedom, the abililty to hack the environment, brutal close-range executions, the return of Liara, and much more.
YouTube content creator Dantics revealed the details in a new video, as he was a member of the Mass Effect Council – a group of external Mass Effect community members who gave BioWare feedback on the game during development. IGN has verified the legitimacy of these details, and can add that a development source told us that BioWare had "every major [alien] race" working in the build.
Dantics says it "looked incredible" and added, "From what I saw, BioWare was making Mass Effect for us, the fans." More specifically, he shared that the new Mass Effect was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and your customizable agent was like a John Wick/James Bond-type character who has had experimental technology implanted in you. As a result, you'd be able to hack and manipulate the environment such as letting you "see through walls, identify systems, remotely trigger hazards, and more." Furthermore, you'd also be able to perform "brutal, close-range executions."
Meanwhile, the galaxy has been divided into three major factions, with humanity, the Krogans, the Batarians, and others allied together. The Council races formed their own alliance, while the Geth had emerged as a third superpower who constructed megastructures. Dantics describes the setting of Mass Effect Universe as "a galactic Cold War instead of another Reaper-style invasion with a shadowy adversary."
Missions would've been handcrafted, like in the original trilogy, "but with Hitman-style freedom in how you complete them." Your squadmates would be able to clash with each other, while romance options would return without being "sanitized." Finally, Liara would return from the original trilogy, now as a powerful Asari Matriarch.
BioWare's closure and Mass Effect 5's cancellation have saddened many in the gaming community. I wrote a eulogy about how BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever. Our own Jackie Thomas lamented that we'll never get to see the series redeemed after the disappointment of Mass Effect Andromeda, and IGN's Matt Purslow believed that EA never knew what it had with BioWare. An internal trailer leaked online following the cancellation that gives us all an idea of what BioWare was building.
Fans aren't giving up yet, though, as an online petition has already surged past 50,000 signatures. In addition, a Canadian politician is calling on the government to support BioWare developers in a buyout that would enable to run the studio independently. We spoke to a number of analysts this week to find out why EA shut BioWare down, and the chances of a franchise selloff.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Immersive Gamebox is teaming up with Netflix to bring fans into the world of KPop Demon Hunters. A new interactive gaming experience based on the animated streaming hit will launch across select U.S. locations in January 2027.
item.description:
Immersive Gamebox is teaming up with Netflix to bring fans into the world of KPop Demon Hunters. A new interactive gaming experience based on the animated streaming hit will launch across select U.S. locations in January 2027.
According to a press release, the experience will have players “move, react, and work together through a series of interactive games featuring 3D motion tracking, projection mapping, touch-sensitive walls and spatial audio.” The experience avoids heavy VR goggles, instead using lightweight motion-tracking headsets.
Before getting into actual gameplay, players will get to create their own ‘Superfan’ avatar in the style of the animated movie. Then, HUNTR/X will guide participants on a quest to protect the Honmoon. The experience will feature familiar locations, moments, and characters from the movie while requiring participants to work together on minigames and activities.
The full KPop Demon Hunters experience is designed for two to six players with an estimated run time of 60 minutes. Tickets will be available in December, but fans can already sign up to join a Priority Waitlist that will offer 24 hours of early access before the general sale.
Immersive Gamebox launched in London before opening its first U.S. location in 2020. The company really hit its stride with licensed collaborations, having previously worked with Netflix on its Squid Game and Floor Is Lava experiences. It now hosts over 29 experiences at 35 venues.
“KPop Demon Hunters perfectly captures what we do best: transforming the world’s most exciting stories into shared experiences that friends and families can play together," said Lisa Paton, CEO of Immersive Gamebox. "Music, movement, and the collective energy of the fans are such a huge part of this film, and we can’t wait for fans to join the action and become part of the story.”
This isn’t fans’ only opportunity to help Huntr/x protect the Honmoon. Netflix will be hosting its own KPop Demon Hunters: The Immersive Experience at two Netflix House locations this November. The Netflix experience will make use of "3D technology" while also featuring live actors, multiple sets, and themed food and drinks.
Both immersive experiences will stick to the movie's original Honmoon story, though we'll be getting more action in the world of KPop Demon Hunters soon enough. Well, maybe not too soon. Reports suggest the sequel may not release until at least 2029. At the very least, Netflix has already agreed to correct its previous mistakes by giving KPop Demon Hunters 2 a full theatrical release.
ICYMI: Netflix and LEGO recently teamed up on a giant KPop Demon Hunters build.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Inde Navarrette revealed a sneak peek at her Rogue accent in a new video featuring her take on the X-Men hero's iconic "sugar" catchphrase, but she's willing to "work on it" if fans don't like it.
item.description:
Inde Navarrette revealed a sneak peek at her Rogue accent in a new video featuring her take on the X-Men hero's iconic "sugah" catchphrase, but she's willing to "work on it" if fans don't like it.
One of the many stars confirmed to appear in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie gave fans a taste of the big reveal that everyone's been waiting on: her take on Rogue's accent. Navarrette offered just a single "sugah" when asked for a tease during an interview with Etalk at TIFF 2026 last month.
The Obsession breakout admitted she's not "done a lot of practice" when it comes to her Rogue preparation, but it looks like she has spent at least some time fitting a more recognizable word from her vocabulary into her performance. You can see the clip of Navarrette in question below.
Rogue is known for her sense of style and power-sapping abilities, but it might be her accent that fans know her for best. With Navarrette confirmed to play the Mississippi-born mutant when X-Men joins the MCU in 2028, fans have been dying to hear what she'll sound like – and she knows it.
In September, she assured Rogue fans that she was putting in the work to, above all else, nail that Southern delivery. Part of her plan to do so involved planning a trip to Mississippi at some point in the future, saying at the time that "Southern women are really my favorite." She also went on to say that she was "doing everything humanly possible" to do Rogue justice because she "loves that character."
Rogue has appeared in animated and live-action form before, but her introduction into the MCU could be her most important portrayal yet. Navarrette is all too aware of what she and her roots mean to fans, so if you don't like that quick "sugah" she teased last month, she promised she'll iron out the kinks with Marvel Studios.
"I that, you know, I'm going to work on it if you don't like it," she said, "and I'm going to figure out and talk to the Marvel team on what we want to do."
Following months of Mystique rumors, Navarrette was confirmed to play Rogue when Marvel appeared for a special announcement at D23 in August. She was joined by a host of other cast confirmations, including Christopher Abbott as Professor X and Maya Boyd as Storm, too. Asa Germann was cast as Angel not much longer after.
X-Men will reimagine classic Marvel superheroes for the big screen when it comes to theaters May 5, 2028. Until then, you can see how Rogue's animated voice actor, Lenore Zann, reacted to Navarrette's casting. You can also read up on the comic book stories director Jake Schreier is keeping in mind while working on the project.

item.title: Innovative and prolific Nintendo game developer Shigeru Miyamoto will receive Japan’s highest honor for cultural merit next month. The 73-year old is the first video game developer to receive the Order of Culture, which is presented by the Emperor of Japan.
item.description:
Legendary Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto will receive Japan’s highest honor for cultural merit next month. The 73-year old is the first video game developer to receive the Order of Culture, which is presented by the Emperor of Japan.
“I feel incredibly awkward but truly honored to be selected for such a prestigious award,” Miyamoto told the press on October 23. “As I often point out, I don’t create games on my own. This award is the result of working together with a great number of people, so I will accept it on their behalf.”
“Recently, I’ve been privileged to work with people from many different fields, not just games,” he added, referencing Super Nintendo World attractions at Universal Studios and films like The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. “I’d like to share the joy of this award with everyone.”
Miyamoto is currently Nintendo’s Executive Fellow and Representative Director. He joined the company in 1977, playing a pivotal and formative role in Nintendo’s move towards making video games. While most famous for creating the Mario series (with the iconic Nintendo mascot’s first appearance in 1981’s Donkey Kong), Miyamoto also played key roles in the development of other major Nintendo franchises including The Legend of Zelda and Star Fox.
“50 years ago, I became involved in video games, a medium whose form was still very undefined, and I have been fortunate to continue in this line of work ever since.” Miyamoto said. “I feel like it’s precisely because I’ve been here since the dawn of the industry that I’m being honored in this way, and think I have been incredibly lucky in life.”
Japan’s Order of Culture, as the name suggests, is awarded to individuals deemed to have made outstanding contributions to the development of culture. It covers a broad scope, from the sciences to literature and the arts. Previous well-known recipients include film director Akira Kurosawa, fashion designer Issey Miyake, and Godzilla composer Akira Ifukube.
The Emperor of Japan will present Miyamoto and the other seven recipients with their Order of Culture awards. Like in previous years, the ceremony will be held on November 3, Japan’s Culture Day national holiday.
Photo by Kevin Winter/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images.
Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

item.title: EA seems to have quietly pulled a collection of Mass Effect content for Battlefield 6 just days after it shuttered series developer BioWare.
item.description:
EA seems to have quietly pulled a collection of Mass Effect content for Battlefield 6 just days after it shuttered series developer BioWare.
Battlefield 6 players made a mental note of an incoming Mass Effect collab when themed content was added to cosmetic menus with the launch of Season 5 earlier this month. As captured and shared by fans across social media, the previously locked crossover collection featured some sci-fi weaponry, a Normandy ship weapon charm, and more N7-branded items.
With a Dead Space crossover having been added at the same time and N7 Day just around the corner, fans suspected they wouldn't have to wait long to get their hands on the new content. Some even suggested the surprise drop meant EA might have plans to deliver an update on its long-in-development Mass Effect 5 project. Of course, the controversial game publisher announced just days ago that it had no plans for BioWare or Mass Effect at all.
There's new Mass Effect accessories for Battlefield, probably for N7 Day 👀 https://t.co/n7cAHFUSHz
The remaining team of developers at the studio were abruptly laid off when the studio was shut down two days ago, October 21, 2026. It was a move that rocked the industry and left both fans and outsiders bewildered as EA also confirmed Mass Effect 5 was canceled, with the series' gaming presence consequently thrown into an indefinite hiatus. Perhaps more confusing was the existence of that Mass Effect content in Battlefield 6, but it didn't take long for DICE and the rest of BioWare's former sister studios at Battlefield Studios to pull the collaboration completely.
Fans quickly discovered EA had quietly removed any mention of the Mass Effect cosmetics in the wake of BioWare's shutdown. Although it's a move that has only further divided a community of gamers already disheartened by EA leadership, it's easy to see why the company swiftly moved to pull the plug.
Continuing to push Mass Effect content on fans mourning the demise of the once-beloved sci-fi RPG franchise would certainly only sour the already-bitter taste in players' mouths. With there likely being no plans for any of the franchise's usual N7 Day festivities come November 7, a relatively small drop of cosmetics would have only added insult to injury.
It would have been an especially painful blow for fans of EA's past considering the publisher already caught flak for its even more prominent Dead Space crossover. Featuring both weapons and even a new mode, Battlefield 6's collab arrived at a time when Dead Space's future as a living, breathing game franchise also remained a mystery. Although franchise followers seem to have enjoyed the mode, many have also lobbed criticism at EA for doing the minimum with some of its most critically acclaimed IP.
Still, there are those who think the Mass Effect cosmetics, which seem to have been finished and ready for launch at any moment, would have still been nice to have. After all, the franchise isn't completely without a plan, at least for now. Amazon's Prime Video, for example, confirmed to IGN its previously announced Mass Effect TV series was still very much in the works following BioWare's closure. There are also those hoping the IP and even some members of its studio's team of developers could find a new home.
EA was officially acquired by Saudi Arabia's PIF, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners in August of this year. Some analysts believe the decision to close the BioWare was "entirely predictable." For now, BioWare and the Mass Effect game franchise seem to be without a future. In the wake of decision making by EA leadership, fans quickly launched a petition to save the series and amassed more than 50,000 signatures. A trailer for the now-canceled Mass Effect 5 also quickly leaked online.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Amazon has announced an official title for its Fallout Shelter reality competition show, and a Prime Video release date.
item.description:
Amazon has announced a January 13, 2027 release date for its reality competition show, Fallout Shelter: The Experiment.
Confirmation comes via a short video that shows a Pip-Boy displaying the message: “The world is ending. The competition is just beginning.”
Good morning, future Vault Dwellers! Please Stand By for an important announcement. Fallout Shelter: The Experiment — an all-new competition series — arrives January 13, only on @primevideo. https://t.co/U87TSfNayV
Fallout Shelter the video game is Bethesda’s strategy spinoff in which you manage a vault and its dwellers while under constant pressure from the wasteland. Here's the official blurb on the 10-episode series:
Fallout Shelter: The Experiment is produced by Studio Lambert, the company that’s also behind The Traitors and Squid Game: The Challenge, with Kilter Films, and in association with Bethesda Game Studios. Todd Howard is down as executive producer.
The release date announcement comes on Fallout Day, (October 23, 2077 is of course the day in the Fallout timeline when the bombs fell, sparking The Great War that caused the irradiated wasteland fans of the franchise have been playing in over the last few decades). This week, Bethesda made a number of relatively low-key announcements, including eye-catching mods for Fallout 4 and some fun real-world collaborations.
Fallout’s 30th anniversary arrives next year, so expect more from Bethesda then. What’s it working on? It’s got everything from Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters to Fallout 5, with an Obsidian-developed Fallout spinoff thrown in for good measure. Work continues on Fallout 76 and Fallout Shelter, and Season 3 of the Fallout TV series is also incoming. In short, Microsoft is doubling down on Fallout, with new Xbox boss Asha Sharma striving for increased profitability across the gaming business.

item.title: EA shut down BioWare on Wednesday, cancelling its upcoming Mass Effect game. And, after the trailer for what's now known as Mass Effect Universe leaked online, fans have started flocking to a petition in the hopes of saving the franchise.
item.description:
EA shut down BioWare on Wednesday, cancelling its upcoming Mass Effect game. And, after the trailer for what's now known as Mass Effect Universe leaked online, fans have started flocking to a petition in the hopes of saving the franchise.
The petition, #SaveMassEffect, was started on the same day as BioWare's closure, and has hit 52,783 signatures at the time of writing, surpassing the original goal of 30,000. Rather than asking EA to reinstate BioWare, the petition demands that EA either puts another studio in charge of the franchise and funds the next Mass Effect game's development, or license out the IP so it can live on.
The petition's author, Joe Smith, made the case for saving Mass Effect: "Mass Effect holds a special place in the hearts of millions of players worldwide. Its rich and immersive sci-fi universe, with Commander Shepard leading the iconic crew aboard the Normandy, has captivated gamers for years. However, recent revelations have cast a shadow over its future. The decline in dedicated resources and ambiguous development plans from Electronic Arts (EA) threaten to leave this beloved series at a standstill, jeopardizing its incredible legacy."
Unfortunately, these kinds of petitions normally fail to spark corporate U-turns. And while a former BioWare executive has suggested EA might be more likely to sell the BioWare IP after the studio's closure, analysts disagree.
When IGN asked industry analyst Joost Van Dreunen about the likelihood of BioWare's IP living on, he told us: "In many ways, BioWare's IP is in the same boat as some of the other studios we recently saw being divested. They are all well-known and too expensive for most buyers. Capable publishers like CD Projekt Red already have their hands full with their own projects."
Still, there is at least one politician who wants the Canadian government to help BioWare employees buy out the studio, which would theoretically allow development to continue on Mass Effect Universe. However, that is a bit of a longshot and would likely take years to play out.
While it feels unlikely that Mass Effect will live on, there is a lot of energy behind the effort to keep the franchise alive. Fans have taken to social media en masse to mourn the death of BioWare, and even if Mass Effect never returns, the spirit of the series will likely live on in games like Exodus and The Expanse: Osiris Reborn.
